chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man came to a man.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him, if he was married (muhsan), is the killing (rajm), and if he was not married, then upon him is the Penalty (Hadd).' I said: 'So what is upon the passive one (al-mu'ta)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the killing, in every state, whether he was married or not married.'

key_terms.الْحَدُّ: The fixed legal penalty (typically flogging for unmarried persons)
key_terms.الْقَتْلُ: Death penalty (specifically Rajm/stoning in this context)
key_terms.مُحْصَنٌ: A married person (specifically one who has consummated marriage)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for the active and passive partners in sodomy according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the active and passive partners in sodomy, establishing that the passive partner (al-mu'ta) incurs the death penalty regardless of marital status, a view notably associated with the school of Imam al-Sadiq. It highlights the application of *rajm* (stoning) for the married active partner and *hadd* (flogging) for the unmarried, reflecting the classical Shia legal methodology of deriving specific penalties from prophetic tradition.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘A man comes to a man’. Heasws said: ‘Upon him, if he was married, is the killing, and if does not happen to be married, so upon him would be the Penalty (Hadd)’. I said, ‘So what is upon the passive one?’ Heasws said: ‘Upon him is the killing, upon every state, be he married or without a marriage’.
